clue.text: Finance record of work to be completed

parts.note: to back a venture is to finance it
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A ledger listing jobs still awaiting completion, kept by the finance department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finance record' reads as an accounts book, but the two words are separate pieces; 'of' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is an accumulation of tasks still waiting to be dealt with.

clue.text: Displaying a lumbering tread — until point of disappearance

indicators.note: displaying here means putting the letters out on show in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone plods heavily along right up to the spot where things vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lumbering' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder: all fifteen letters of A LUMBERING TREAD are rearranged; 'until' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of the western Atlantic is notorious in legend for ships and aircraft vanishing without trace.

clue.text: Bore's degree of suitability

definitions.meaning: the internal diameter of a gun barrel

explanation.definitionFit: Calibre is both the diameter of a gun's barrel and a measure of someone's quality or worth.

clue.text: Viewer in house let rent go spiralling

indicators.note: spiralling suggests letters whirling round into a new order

explanation.surface: A landlord lets rent rise out of control in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' means a theatre or opera house, where the viewing aid is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles on a handle, traditionally used at the opera or theatre.

clue.text: Rejoiced in getting lost on run, in early dawn starts

indicators.note: starts tells us to take the opening letter of each word in the run before it

explanation.surface: Someone rejoiced at getting lost while running at daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' joins definition to wordplay, as in 'gloried in'; the second 'in' is one of the words whose initial is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To glory in something is to take great pride or delight in it, to exult.

clue.text: Rush last editions onto overnight van

indicators.note: onto places the single letter on the front of the vehicle that follows
last points to the final letter of the word editions

parts.note: a camper is a van fitted out for sleeping in overnight

explanation.surface: Late newspaper editions are hurriedly loaded onto a van for night delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like an instruction about the newspapers; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run with quick light steps, to scurry.

clue.text: Deception achieved by putting energy into insult

indicators.note: putting one thing into another means placing the letter inside the word for insult

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone tricks others by delivering an insult with real force.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is trickery or cunning, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Hate to see sailor at half anchor

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: half asks for one half of the word anchor, here its back three letters

explanation.surface: A sailor recoils at seeing the anchor only half raised.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to loathe or detest it.

clue.text: Acclaim of two raised in mine

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: dual means having two parts, of two

explanation.surface: Two miners are hoisted up a pit shaft to great acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' works only because this is a down clue: the word for 'of two' is written upwards, giving a word meaning praise, and 'mine' surrounds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or approval.

clue.text: Dangerous gamble for two boys on spinning wheel

parts.note: Russ is a boy's name, the first of the two
Ian is a boy's name, the second of the two
roulette is the casino game played on a spinning wheel

explanation.surface: Two lads bet recklessly on a turning wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning wheel' suggests a device for making yarn, but it is the casino wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The deadly game of firing a revolver with one loaded chamber at one's head stands for any reckless risk.

clue.text: One who has power is left in regret — right?

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for regret

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A question whether a powerful figure is left feeling sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a sovereign or governor who exercises authority.

clue.text: Leaders chasing completed costs

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the leaders follow the completed word

parts.note: over means finished or completed
heads are leaders, as heads of department

explanation.surface: Front runners pursue those who have finished, at some cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Overheads are a business's regular running expenses, such as rent and lighting.

clue.text: Stiff British taken in by interminable…

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the word that follows

parts.note: unending means interminable

explanation.surface: A rigid Briton is drawn into an endless broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie the clue's surface to the next one; they play no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbending means rigid, inflexible, refusing to yield.

clue.text: …broadcast, failing to finish one's lines

indicators.note: failing to finish means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: radio is broadcasting
one is I, the Roman numeral, with the 's as 'has'

explanation.surface: A radio programme fails to reach the end of someone's script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like an actor's script; it means straight lines from a circle's centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii are the straight lines drawn from the centre of a circle to its circumference.

clue.text: Helped a gamble? Time eliminated doubtful starters

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

indicators.note: starters tells us to take the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A wager is questioned after a time limit knocked out the dubious runners.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the surface; 'a gamble' gives A BET.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Can be enclosing letter from Greek national

indicators.note: enclosing means the word for can wraps around the Greek letter

parts.note: a tin is a can
beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A tin can carries a Greek letter for a citizen of one country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be' is a link: the can 'is to be' enclosing the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tibetan is a person from Tibet, a native of that region.

clue.text: Second grade? Single friend in Derby, perhaps

parts.note: B is the second grade after A
one means single
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from 'china plate'

explanation.surface: An unmarried pal ranked second-class living in Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Crown Derby is a famous English porcelain maker, so Derby is an example; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Crown Derby is one well-known make of fine translucent porcelain made with bone ash.

clue.text: Rufus studied without a brain

indicators.note: without means the letter A is removed from the word for studied

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
head is used informally for brain or intellect

explanation.surface: Someone named Rufus did his studying without any brains.
explanation.walkthrough: Rufus is Latin for red-haired, the nickname of King William II of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufus means red-haired, so it describes a person with ginger hair.

clue.text: Hung over? Inclined to start drinking first

indicators.note: first places that letter at the front of the next piece
start points to the opening letter of the word drinking

parts.note: angled means inclined or sloping

explanation.surface: Feeling hungover? That's what comes of being inclined to start drinking early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hung over' suggests a hangover; it means suspended over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspended loosely over an edge or a drop has swung there.

clue.text: Take away the urge to hold English coins

indicators.note: to hold means the word for urge contains the letters that follow

parts.note: drive is urge or impulse
P stands for pence, British coins

explanation.surface: To remove the desire to keep English money.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone is to take something away from them.

clue.text: Fruit to draw divine being in

indicators.note: draw, completed by 'in', means to pull something inside the little word

parts.note: an angel is a divine being

explanation.surface: Picking up a fruit to sketch a heavenly figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw ... in' is the container signal; 'draw' suggests sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Trot in explosive missile

indicators.note: in places the word for trot inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, an explosive
to trot is to ride a horse at a trot

explanation.surface: A horse trotting into an exploding missile.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is the name of a submarine-launched ballistic missile.

clue.text: Cleared some prospective MP tied to…

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Some would-be politicians are cleared once linked to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To empty a room is to clear it out.

clue.text: Cancel every year, without a…

indicators.note: without means the letter A is dropped from the word

parts.note: annual means happening every year

explanation.surface: Cancelling something every year without a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare invalid or void.

clue.text: …lifting royal drink

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: regal means royal

explanation.surface: A royal raising a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light, fizzy type of beer.

clue.text: …leading actor or capital

definitions.meaning: the star or main performer in a play or ballet
a sum of money invested or lent, as opposed to interest

explanation.definitionFit: Principal names both a lead performer and an original sum of money on which interest is paid.

clue.text: Explosive stage comeback set off…

indicators.note: comeback means the word for stage is read backwards

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
ignite means to set off, fire up

explanation.surface: An explosive theatrical comeback is triggered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' suggests theatre; it is a stage of a journey, a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is a high explosive made from nitroglycerine.

clue.text: …fool and bird hit out, dropping the odds

indicators.note: dropping the odds means only the even-placed letters of the words are kept

explanation.surface: A fool and a bird lash out, both losing their bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link; the letters come from 'bird hit out' only.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Finish treatment for sore back

parts.note: end means finish

indicators.note: treatment for means the letters of sore are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Complete the therapy for a sore back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the body part; it means support.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a proposal is to back or support it.

clue.text: Turkeys start to walk like ducks? Rubbish

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the word Turkeys

parts.note: to waddle is to walk with short swaying steps like a duck

explanation.surface: Turkeys trying to walk like ducks is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly or pretentious talk, nonsense.
